content:
Formula: Product Rule for Differentiation
Exact Expression: \frac{d}{dx}[u(x)v(x)] = u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x)
Definitions: Derivative of the product of two differentiable functions equals derivative of the first times second plus first times derivative of the second.
Derivation/Reference: Derived via limit definition of derivative: lim_{h->0} [u(x+h)v(x+h) - u(x)v(x)]/h; Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1684)
Example: d/dx [x^2 * sin(x)] = 2x*sin(x) + x^2*cos(x)
Domain: calculus
Assumptions: u and v are differentiable at point x
Common Errors: Mistakenly claiming (uv)' = u'v'
subject: Product Rule for Differentiation
